A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same π-Flow work. All 27 pages of each version, including Appendices A–G, are readable and matchable; text extraction and rendered-page comparison support a reliable assessment.

before.justification: v2 reports original ImageNet and text-to-image experiments in Section 5, plus ablations and a 200-image human preference study in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including ImageNet generation scores and the Appendix D preference study reporting 59.5% preference for π-Flow.

M1.justification: The DX and GMFlow policies, imitation-distillation loss, rollout procedures, dropout, trajectory mixing, and micro-window matching are unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendices B–C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet, captioned-image training data, COCO-10k, HPSv2, and OneIG-Bench coverage. The appendix toy experiments and human preference study are also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the ImageNet and text-to-image experiments, including the separate FLUX.1 schnell comparison in Appendix D. SenseFlow remains the same evaluated baseline; only its citation metadata changes.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Tables 8–9 retain the same resolutions, prompt counts, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and hyperparameters. The appendix evaluation procedures and preference-study sample size are unchanged.

E4.justification: The dropout, policy-family, temperature, and micro-window ablations are unchanged. Both versions also retain the same convergence analysis, factorization experiment, teacher-blur examples, and FLUX.1 schnell failure cases.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate and convergence-curve reporting. Neither reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and no seed or run-count information is added.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains GM-REPA FIDs of 2.85 at 1 NFE and 1.97 at 2 NFEs, and Appendix D retains the 59.5% preference result.

T1.justification: Section 4 replaces the explicit description of epsilon as average imitation error '(velocity error × substep size)' with 'average imitation error per step,' removing the specific velocity-to-step-error identification. The stated asymptotic bounds, convergence assertion, theorems, and Appendix E–F proofs and derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about policy-based generation, simple on-policy distillation, scalability, diversity preservation, and teacher alignment.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning diversity collapse, teacher alignment, GMFlow robustness, and FLUX teacher limitations are unchanged. No substantive applicability boundary, failure explanation, or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, implementation descriptions, hyperparameter tables, hardware timing information, and the repository access link are unchanged. The SenseFlow bibliography update does not change this work's reproducibility information.

R1.justification: SenseFlow's reference changes from a 2025 arXiv entry to ICLR 2026, with corresponding citation-year updates. It is the same cited work; citation membership and substantive research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Preprint' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'; version/date and SenseFlow bibliographic text are updated. Section 4 receives the localized imitation-error wording edit, without broader rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: The edits produce localized line wrapping in Section 4 and reference-list reflow on page 12, alongside updated header presentation. All 13 figures and 10 tables retain their content, structure, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: The scientific evidence, main claims, reproducibility information, and appendix proofs are unchanged. Publication metadata updates and the less specific epsilon description in Section 4 do not establish a meaningful overall improvement or deterioration.
